name: The Medina
tagline: UNESCO-listed old town built by Andalusi refugees
description: Tetouan's whitewashed medina is one of Morocco's best-preserved, shaped by Muslims and Jews fleeing Spain after the Reconquista. Narrow alleys, artisan workshops, and the sprawling souks make it a living UNESCO site rather than a tourist reconstruction, though faux guides and vendor hassle are common for visibly foreign visitors.
bestFor: short-term stays, culture and history immersion
cons: easy to get lost in the alleys

name: The Ensanche
tagline: Spanish-built quarter around Place Moulay el Mehdi
description: Built during the Spanish protectorate era, the Ensanche is Tetouan's modern center, with wide boulevards, Art Deco buildings, and most of the city's cafes, banks, and shops. This is the practical base for remote workers, closest to workable wifi, restaurants, and grand taxi stands, with a calmer, more orderly feel than the medina.
bestFor: remote work, longer stays, daily errands
pros: best cafe and wifi access in the city
cons: can feel generic compared to the medina

name: Martil
description: A relaxed seaside town about 10 km from Tetouan, Martil is the default beach escape for locals and visitors alike, with a long sandy beach and a promenade of seafood restaurants and cafes. It gets lively in summer with domestic tourists and quiets down considerably the rest of the year, making it a seasonal rather than year-round base.

name: M'diq
tagline: Small marina town and Tetouan's other nearby coast option
description: A bit further than Martil at roughly 15 km, M'diq is a smaller, tidier resort town with a marina, a walkable corniche, and a slightly more upscale feel. It draws both Moroccan and cross-strait Spanish visitors and offers a quieter alternative to Martil with decent restaurant options along the water.
